chunks: A group of my scholars, including my father, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ali ibn al-Husayn, all narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd al-Yaqṭīnī, from Abī 'Abdillāh Zakariyyā al-Mu'min, from Abī Muskān, from Zayd, the freedman of Ibn Hubayrah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) said: Hold on to the belt of this 'Anza' (the empty one), for he is the greatest Truthful One (Ṣiddīq Akbar) and the guide for whoever follows him. Whoever precedes him has apostatized from the religion of Allah. Whoever abandons him, Allah will destroy him. Whoever adheres to him has adhered to Allah [adhered to the Cord of Allah]. Whoever accepts his Wilayah, Allah guides him; and whoever neglects his Wilayah, Allah leads him astray. From him are the two chiefs of my nation, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and they are my sons. From the descendants of al-Ḥusayn are the guided Imams and the Qā'im al-Mahdī. Therefore, love them and be loyal to them, and do not take their enemies as allies instead of them, for if you do, the wrath of your Lord will befall you and humiliation in the worldly life. And he who forges a lie has certainly failed.

key_terms.الْأَنْزَعِ: The empty one (a title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.سِبْطَا أُمَّتِي: The two chiefs of my nation

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the title 'Anza' and 'Ṣiddīq Akbar' for Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, presents a chain of transmission linking the Prophet Muhammad to Imam Ali (a.s.) as the 'Anza' (the one with the empty hand, symbolizing reliance on God) and the 'Ṣiddīq Akbar,' establishing his primacy in faith. It explicitly connects the Imamate to the Prophet's progeny, identifying Hasan and Husayn as the 'Sibtayn' (two ribbons/parts) of the Ummah, and traces the line of guided Imams through Husayn to the Mahdi, thereby grounding Shia theological authority in prophetic lineage and divine guidance.
